<!-- Generated by tools/export_results.py. Edit only the Experiment and Observations sections. -->

## Experiment

Standardized 50-pair `flash` `coop --git` baseline on `vertex_ai/gemini-3.8-flash` (`low` thinking — matching the `flash` model setup in `notes/model_thinking_stepcounter_flash10.md` — 100 steps, compaction at 28K, per-turn step counter, `$40` per-agent cost cap). Serves as the full-scale control arm for the `gemini-3.8-flash` winning communication intervention (`coop-msa_v2-git-gemini-3-8-flash-flash-low-intents`), and compares directly against the 36/50 (72%) `solo` saturation ceiling.

## Observations

- Passed **27/50 (54.0%)** (`$33.95`, 169 min wall time), an **18 percentage-point coordination drop** below the 36/50 (72.0%) `solo` saturation run on the same 50 pairs. 26 of the 27 passes merged cleanly (`clean` or `identical`), with only 7 merge conflicts across all 50 pairs (compared with 24 conflicts on `gemini-3-flash-preview`), showing that `gemini-3.8-flash`'s primary `coop` bottleneck is semantic coordination and step-budget exhaustion rather than raw git edit collisions.
- Agents sent 1,280 messages total (25.6 per pair) across 7,996 steps and 143 compactions, with 12 of 100 agents stopping at the 100-step limit and zero agent crashes.
- **Concurrency note (`-c 10`)**: At 20 concurrent agents, `vertex_ai/gemini-3.8-flash` experienced 25 `429` rate-limit retries and 2 `503` server-busy retries (up to ~600s server-side queuing per stalled call), causing 32.6% of blocking `send_message --wait` calls (`14/43`) to time out after 60s before receiving an asynchronous reply (`0` false peer-unreachable notices occurred in this baseline). Prefer `-c 4` for future 50-pair `gemini-3.8-flash` runs.
